```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY once this note is published: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  "The number of possible random assignments is restated three orders of magnitude too large",
  "published p. 162",
  "would map each of the [[30 trillion]] random assignments onto just two potential outcomes",
  "would map each of the [[34 billion]] random assignments onto just two potential outcomes",
  paste("Two sentences earlier, on p. 161, the article gives the same quantity as",
        "$2^{35} = 3.4 \\times 10^{10}$, which the deposit confirms: 35 matched pairs, so",
        "34,359,738,368 possible assignments. Thirty trillion is $3 \\times 10^{13}$."),
  "method_assignments_trillion"
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  stopifnot(n >= 1, n <= length(words))
  words[n]
}

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

This note lists `r spell(nrow(entries))` correction to "Information Spillovers: Another Look at Experimental Estimates of Legislator Responsiveness," published in *Journal of Experimental Political Science* 1(2):159--169, doi [10.1017/xps.2014.9](https://doi.org/10.1017/xps.2014.9). **It changes no estimate and no conclusion**: it is a count stated correctly once and misstated two sentences later.

Separately, the upper confidence bounds in the article and its appendix each sit one grid step too high, because the deposited code reports the first hypothesis outside each 95% region rather than the last one inside it; the maintained code corrects the rule, and no conclusion the article draws from those bounds changes.

The article's substantive correction is the 2016 corrigendum, *Journal of Experimental Political Science* 3(2):206--208, doi [10.1017/XPS.2016.8](https://doi.org/10.1017/XPS.2016.8), which this note supplements and does not replace. The code supporting the maintained analysis, which reproduces both the article and the corrigendum, is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2014](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2014).

# The text

```{r text-entries, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
walk(entries$entry, function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
